authoredNote: Source written first from the #867 ruling (ownerName = innermost enclosing DECLARATION); the expectation's kind/owner spellings and edge lines were recorded from the post-ruling run. java already satisfied the ruling before it — this fixture's job is to hold java to it, since nothing pinned the anon type's owner for any language.
rationale: M49/M37 #867. The census measured the four JVM analyzers disagreeing on which DECLARATION owns an anonymous type declared inside a method: java/groovy/scala said the method, kotlin said the class. Ruled: the innermost enclosing declaration, and kotlin was changed. Both contexts are pinned so the fixture cannot be satisfied by a blanket re-owning: a class-level literal is owned by the CLASS (first block) and an in-method literal by the METHOD (second block), and each crossed containment edge is forbidden.
